## Office Action Analysis and Response Drafting

Map every rejection in a USPTO office action to the claims, limitations, and cited passages behind it, then build the response on the signed analysis. Quotations are checked against the source text, amendments are linked to support in the application as filed, and the response is approved by an attorney before it is exported for filing.

### From Examiner Rejection to an Attorney-Approved Response

### One-Click Issue Map

Grounds of rejection, affected claims, and cited references are read from the action once an attorney confirms the documents.

### Source-Checked Claim Charts

Every limitation is charted against its cited passages, and each quotation is matched to the source text before it is stored.

### Supported Claim Amendments

Choose a strategy for every issue, amend the claim listing, and link inserted words to the application as filed.

### Attorney Sign-Off and Approval

An attorney signs the analysis, and the response is approved by an attorney who did not last revise it, then locked.

Built for USPTO office actions today, with EP planned next. AI drafting aids depend on capability availability and workspace policy.

## FDA 21 CFR Part 11-Aligned Controls, Built In, Not Bolted On

Every regulated workflow is built around traceability, approval control, and immutable records. Capture reasons for change, preserve audit history, require review checkpoints, and keep every edit tied to a user, timestamp, and record.

### Reason-for-Change on Every Edit

Critical field edits require a documented reason before saving. No silent changes.

### Full Audit Trail

Every change logged: who, what, when, and the before/after diff.

### Electronic Signatures

Re-authentication prompt before approval actions and high-risk operations.

### Append-Only Audit Records

Audit history is append-only. The application exposes no edit or delete path, so records stay read-only.

### Role-Based Access Control

Admin, Attorney, Paralegal, Viewer: granular permissions enforced server-side.

### Secure Document Management

Version-controlled uploads with presigned downloads and full delete audit trail.

## Six Layers of Compliance-Native Defense

Every patent record, draft, fee event, and audit log is protected through layered controls, from confidential AI processing to tenant-scoped queries and enforced row-level security.

01 Enforced Row-Level Security Database-level access policies help prevent cross-tenant exposure, even from accidental or rogue queries.

02 Strict Tenant Isolation Tenant-scoped transactions keep every organization's patent families, filings, documents, and users separated.

03 Append-Only Audit Trails Every critical mutation records actor, timestamp, reason-for-change, and before/after values.

04 Granular RBAC Admin, Attorney, Paralegal, and Viewer roles control access by module and action.

05 Enterprise SSO Auth0 Organizations, SAML/OIDC, and tenant-level identity controls for enterprise teams.

06 Confidential AI Processing AI drafting and office action drafting aids run on enterprise providers configured so invention data is processed only to produce the output you requested, under the applicable provider agreements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about Design Your Invention. Can't find what you're looking for? Contact our team.

What is Design Your Invention?

Design Your Invention (DYI) is an intellectual property management software (IPMS) platform for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms. It brings multi-jurisdiction patent docketing, prior art search across 100+ patent authorities via the EPO, and AI-assisted patent drafting for US, EP, IN, and PCT (WO) into one connected, audit-trailed workspace. The architecture follows FDA 21 CFR Part 11 patterns, with tenant-scoped data isolation so each organization keeps its portfolio separate.

Is the platform generally available or in private beta?

The full IP management platform is in private beta and under active development, so features can change during the beta. The public patent search tool is live and free to use today. If you want early access to the platform, book a demo or use the contact form and we will talk through your workflow and the current beta scope.

Who is Design Your Invention for?

DYI is built for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms that manage patent portfolios across multiple jurisdictions. Typical users include IP attorneys, patent paralegals, IP directors, and legal operations teams who need patent docketing, prior art search, fee and deadline tracking, and a defensible audit trail in one place, instead of spreadsheets and email.

What is IP management software?

IP management software is a specialized platform that helps law firms, corporations, and patent teams manage their intellectual property portfolios, including patent applications, PCT filings, office actions, deadlines, fees, and compliance requirements. It replaces spreadsheets and email-based tracking with a structured, searchable, and auditable system.

Which controls support an FDA 21 CFR Part 11-aligned workflow?

Every edit to a critical field requires a documented reason-for-change. The audit trail logs who made each change, what changed, and when, and is append-only: the application exposes no edit or delete path on audit history. Electronic approvals require re-authentication, and role-based access control limits who can perform sensitive actions. These are product capabilities, not a compliance certification. Validation and Part 11 compliance depend on each customer intended use, configuration, procedures, training, and quality system.

Can I manage PCT and PRV filings in one place?

Yes. The platform links PRV (provisional), PCT (international), and NPE (national phase entry) cases to their parent patent families. You can see the entire filing hierarchy in a visual family tree, track deadlines across all filing types, and manage office actions and fees from a single dashboard.

Can the platform manage patents across multiple jurisdictions?

Yes. Multi-jurisdiction portfolios are the core use case. Docketing covers US, PCT, EP, JP, CN, and IN, with PRV, PCT, and NPE cases linked to their parent application families so the full filing hierarchy is visible in one place. Deadlines, fees, and office actions are tracked across every jurisdiction in your portfolio, and fee analytics roll up spend with date-accurate multi-currency conversion into one reporting currency.

How does the platform help reduce deadline risk?

Supported statutory and procedural deadlines are derived from your case data rather than entered by hand, so they do not depend on someone remembering to add them to a calendar. Every deadline gets a 0 to 100 risk score with green, amber, and red levels, and automated email digests push what is due to the responsible owner before the date. A weekly stale-alert report also surfaces cases that are quietly going wrong without generating a hard deadline. Calculated dates are workflow aids: coverage depends on the case data you record, and a qualified patent professional remains responsible for verifying every date.

## Patent Docketing and Deadline Management Software
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/docketing#main-content)

# Patent Docketing That Reduces Deadline Risk

One missed annuity payment or office-action response can cost a client an entire patent. Docketing is built as an audit-first engine that derives supported statutory and procedural deadlines from your case data, scores each one by risk, and pushes it to the responsible owner before it comes due. Every calculated date stays reviewable, and remains subject to verification by a qualified patent professional.

## Every Computed Date Shows Its Work

Supported PCT and U.S. office-action deadlines are calculated from recorded case events using deterministic, versioned rules. Review the trigger, citation, arithmetic, calendar adjustment, assumptions, and rule version behind every result.

### Reply to final U.S. Office Action

Illustrative calculation

Rule version

2026.08

Coverage

U.S. Office Action

Trigger source

Attorney-entered

- Trigger Office Action issued July 24, 2026 Attorney-entered case event

- Rule 3-month shortened statutory period 35 U.S.C. 133 · 37 CFR 1.113, 1.116, 1.136(a)

- Calculation July 24 + 3 calendar months October 24 falls on Saturday

- USPTO calendar Rolled to Monday, October 26

- Computed due date October 26, 2026

### Cited and explainable

See the source event, governing authority, assumptions, and every calculation step.

### Attorney control is preserved

Overrides retain the computed value, require a reason, and remain fully audited.

### Updates never move dates silently

Preview the impact, review changes, sign the release, and restore the prior version.

## Triage by Real Risk, Not Just Date Order

Every deadline gets a 0 to 100 risk score and a traffic-light level, so attorneys triage by workload pressure rather than date order alone. The score is a weighted blend of four signals, and scores roll up into a portfolio-level breakdown for an at-a-glance health read. Scores rank what needs attention first. They are not a legal assessment of the case.

### Time pressure

How close, or how far past, the deadline is. Overdue items spike toward 100.

### Type severity

Office actions (90) and annuities (80) outrank routine reminders (20).

### Overdue cascade

Already-overdue or open past-due items escalate sharply rather than plateauing.

### Assignment gap

Unassigned deadlines are penalized. An orphaned deadline is a dangerous deadline.

Portfolio rollup

### Risk health at a glance

## Deadlines Come to You, Not the Other Way Around

Docketing does not wait for users to log in. Three automated digest jobs push deadlines out, each respecting user notification preferences, throttled to provider limits, and failing gracefully per user. A fourth report goes further and catches what date-only docketing misses entirely.

### Daily Deadline Digest

Every morning at 8 AM in each tenant local timezone, every user gets the deadlines coming due within a configurable window, pre-sorted by risk.

### Reminder-Due Email

The same morning send for custom reminders falling due that day, so team-specific tasks land alongside statutory deadlines.

### Weekly Stale-Alert Digest

Mondays at 9 AM local, a hygiene report of the things quietly going wrong that no hard deadline would surface.

### Families with no filings

A docket opened but never built out, sitting empty and forgotten.

### Stale records

PRV, PCT, or NPE entities untouched past a threshold (default 90 days).

### Overdue open office actions

Past due and still not responded, the single most expensive thing to miss.

### Unpaid overdue fees

Annuities past due, surfaced with grace-period and amount context.

### Expired reminders

Pending reminders whose date has already passed without action.

### Stale families

Active families with no updates inside the threshold window.

## The Operating Layer Around Every Deadline

Fees, outside counsel, family health, dashboards, and bulk operations all feed the same prioritized deadline view, so the docket reflects how patent work actually flows. The same data becomes a branded PDF report for a client or an auditor, it can leave in a format you own whenever you want it, and it rolls up into the protection horizon of every product it covers.

### Multi-currency fees

Track patent and annuity fees with status, due date, amount, and currency. Analytics roll up spend across the portfolio with date-accurate FX conversion into one chosen currency.

### Outside-counsel directory

A searchable, tenant-scoped roster of firms and agents, with per-case assignments by role (lead counsel, local agent, foreign associate, annuity provider) and duplicate-assignment protection.

### Family completeness scoring

Each family gets a 0 to 100 data-completeness score across family fields, child coverage, and child quality, turning "is this docket set up correctly?" into a measurable number.

### Portfolio dashboard

Status breakdowns across families, PRVs, PCTs, NPE cases, office actions, annuities, and reminders, plus deadline-window counts and the aggregate risk breakdown, as of any chosen date.

### Bulk CSV import

Onboard whole portfolios in one pass, importing families with their PRV, PCT, and NPE child records and key dates, with validation and column mapping.

### Filtering and export

Filter deadlines by type, family, priority, date range, and assignee, with a "mine only" view for limited-permission users. Export deadlines, fees, and entity lists to CSV.

### Branded PDF reports

Turn the live docket into a client-ready document. The portfolio health report carries your logo and organization name, the sections you choose, and an optional as-of date, with deadlines ranked by risk, fees grouped per currency, and stale-record alerts.

### Verifiable report integrity

Every report is stamped with a unique Report ID and a SHA-256 checksum written to your audit log, and the preview and the download are byte identical. A report you handed a client months ago can still be verified against the record.

### Data portability, no lock-in

Export the whole account, not just a view. Families, filings, cases, fees, reminders, and audit history come out as structured NDJSON with schemas and CSV renderings, on every plan. Each user can also export their own personal data from their profile.

## Audit-First, Tenant-Isolated, Built to Survive Review

Docketing inherits the platform multi-tenant, audit-first architecture. The same controls that make the platform defensible in enterprise procurement apply to every reminder, fee, and case.

### Full audit trail

Every create, update, and delete on reminders, fees, and cases is logged with actor, before and after state, timestamp, IP, and request ID. Report generation and data exports are audited the same way, and an account export requires a typed reason and notifies every admin.

### Reason-for-change enforced

Edits to sensitive fields such as dates and statuses require a typed reason, and deletions always do. The field is required rather than optional, following 21 CFR Part 11 patterns.

### Tenant isolation

Every query runs under PostgreSQL Row-Level Security inside a tenant-scoped transaction. Defense-in-depth tenant isolation is designed to prevent one firm from reaching another firm docket.

### Role-based access

Read versus write is enforced server-side per module (prv, pct, npe, and the rest). "View all reminders" versus "only mine" is a permission, not a UI toggle.

## Docketing Questions

How deadlines are derived, scored, and surfaced before they come due.

Is this a calendar I have to keep up to date by hand?

No. Supported deadlines are computed on read from the underlying case records, not entered manually. The moment you set a filing date or a publication date, every dependent statutory and procedural deadline the engine supports appears automatically and recalculates when those source fields change. Dates the engine does not derive stay under your control as custom reminders, and all dates should be verified by a qualified patent professional.

Which deadlines are computed, and which are tracked?

Current computed coverage focuses on supported PCT deadlines and U.S. office-action response chains. Each result carries its informational trust status and a derivation trace, and must be professionally verified. The unified docket also tracks annuities, provisional and national-phase matters, patent fees, and custom reminders; not every tracked date is a rules-based calculation.

How does risk scoring decide what is red?

Every deadline gets a 0 to 100 score blending four signals: time pressure (40%), type severity (25%), overdue cascade (25%), and assignment gap (10%). A score of 70 or higher is red, 40 or higher is amber, and anything lower is green. Scores roll up into a portfolio-level breakdown so managers get an at-a-glance health read. The score prioritizes workflow attention. It is not a legal assessment of the case or of the consequences of a missed date.

Will deadlines look overdue a day early for international teams?

No. "Today" is computed in each tenant local timezone, so a deadline is not miscolored for a team in another part of the world. Annuity fees also track a grace-period end date, so the system separates "overdue but still payable in grace" from "truly lapsed."

What are the email digests, and can users control them?

Three automated jobs push deadlines out: a daily deadline digest (8 AM local, pre-sorted by risk), a reminder-due email the same morning, and a weekly stale-alert hygiene report on Mondays at 9 AM local. Sends respect each user notification preferences, are throttled to provider limits, and fail gracefully per user so one bad address does not block the batch.

What is the stale-alert report for?

It surfaces silent risks that no hard deadline would catch: families with no filings, stale PRV/PCT/NPE records, overdue open office actions, unpaid overdue fees, expired reminders, and stale families. It is the "what is slipping through the cracks?" view that date-only docketing misses.

Can it handle a multi-currency, multi-jurisdiction portfolio?

Yes. Fees and annuities carry an amount and currency, and analytics roll up spend across the portfolio with date-accurate FX conversion into a single chosen reporting currency. Fees attach polymorphically to families, PRV, PCT, NPE cases, or office actions, so renewal exposure is visible at every level.

How is the docket defensible in an audit?

Every create, update, and delete on reminders, fees, and cases is logged with actor, before and after state, timestamp, IP, and request ID. Edits to sensitive fields require a typed reason, deletions always do, and tenant data is isolated with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security. Read versus write is enforced server-side per module.

Can I hand a client or an auditor a report straight from the docket?

Yes. The portfolio health report turns the live docket into a branded PDF in one click. It carries your organization logo and name, only the sections you select, and an optional as-of date, and it covers portfolio stats, family analytics, deadlines ranked by risk, annuity and patent fees grouped per currency, and stale-record alerts. Every report is stamped with a unique Report ID and a SHA-256 checksum written to your audit log, so a document you handed over months ago can still be verified against the record.

Can I see when a drug product actually loses exclusivity?

Yes. The Loss of Exclusivity timeline links each drug product to the patent families and regulatory exclusivities that protect it, then shows three numbers per jurisdiction and indication: the patent wall (the latest granted patent expiry), the regulatory floor (the latest active exclusivity end date), and the combined horizon, which is the later of the two. A live what-if lets you drop a patent family and watch every affected product recompute, so the cost of letting an annuity lapse is visible before the decision is made. The timeline visualizes the dates your attorneys record. It is a portfolio visualization, not a legal determination.

How does it track renewal and annuity fee dates?

Annuity and renewal fees are tracked with amount, currency, due date, fee year, renewal year, and a grace-period end date. The engine derives each renewal deadline automatically from the case data, buckets it by urgency, and the daily digest surfaces it before it comes due, distinguishing "overdue but still payable in grace" from "truly lapsed."

How does it reduce the risk of a missed deadline or human error?

Supported deadlines are computed on read from the case records rather than typed into a calendar, so they do not depend on someone remembering to add them. Unassigned deadlines are penalized in the risk score, abandoned or paid items drop out automatically, and three automated digests push what is due to the responsible owner. The weekly stale-alert report catches cases that are silently going wrong without generating a hard deadline. Accuracy still depends on the case data you record, and calculated dates should be verified by a qualified patent professional.

How hard is it to migrate our existing docket from spreadsheets or another tool?

Most teams start with a bulk CSV import. You upload your existing portfolio and the system validates every row before anything touches the database, then creates families with their PRV, PCT, and NPE child records and key dates in a single atomic transaction with a full audit trail. Supported dependent deadlines appear automatically when the required source dates are imported.

If we ever leave, can we take our data with us?

Yes, on every plan, and without a support ticket. A tenant admin can export the entire account in one click: families, filings, PRV, PCT and NPE cases, office actions, fees, reminders, prior-art references, team roles, and the audit trail. The bundle ships as structured NDJSON with a JSON Schema for every dataset, plus CSV renderings of the common docket views, so it stays readable in Excel and parseable by another system. Each dataset carries a SHA-256 checksum, the whole export is a consistent point-in-time snapshot, and the export itself is audited and emailed to every admin. Individual users can export their own personal data from their profile.

Does it integrate with our existing tools, and is it cloud-based?

It is a cloud web application with nothing to install. Every list view (deadlines, fees, families, PRV, PCT, NPE, and audit logs) supports one-click CSV export, bulk CSV import handles onboarding, and a REST API is available for custom integrations with existing firm systems.

## From Molecule to Clinic, Beside the Patent

Linked trials from ClinicalTrials.gov show phase, status, sponsor, and indication, so you can see what is in clinic for a molecule and who is running it, right beside the patent.

## Patent Search Questions

What the free search covers, and what a work email unlocks.

Is patent search free?

Yes. You can search a corpus of 120M+ patent records from 100+ patent authorities for free, with no account. Signing in with a work email unlocks full-text claims, CSV export, and more results per page, but the core search and the compound and clinical-trial intelligence are free to use.

Do I need an account to search?

No. Anonymous search covers titles and abstracts across the authorities in the corpus and shows detected compounds and linked clinical trials. You only need to sign in with a work email when you want full-text claims or to export results to CSV.

Can I search by assignee, inventor, jurisdiction, and legal status?

Yes. Alongside keyword and claims search, you can search by inventor and by applicant or assignee, then narrow any query by jurisdiction, filing date, and IPC or CPC classification. Every result carries its legal status, so granted patents are easy to tell from pending applications.

Can I search patents by chemical structure or compound?

Yes. Compounds disclosed in a patent are detected and rendered as 2D structures with their InChIKey, IUPAC name, SMILES, and molecular weight. From any compound you can find other patents in the corpus that disclose the same molecule or scaffold. Detection is automated enrichment over third-party chemistry sources, so verify structures and associations against the original patent before relying on them.

Does the platform support pharma and biotech patent research?

Yes. The enrichment layer is built for pharma and biotech work: disclosed compounds are rendered as 2D structures with full chemical identifiers, and patents are linked to their clinical-trial landscape. Non-pharma searches behave exactly the same, they simply do not pick up the chemistry overlay.

What clinical-trial data is shown?

Patents are linked to trials from ClinicalTrials.gov, showing the trial phase, recruitment status, lead sponsor, and indication. This lets you see, at a glance, what is in clinical development for a molecule and who is running it. Patent-to-trial links are inferred from compound and sponsor data and should be confirmed against the trial record.

Can my team export patent results?

Yes. Signed-in work-email users can export search results to CSV for sharing with IP or R&D teams, alongside full-text claims and a higher per-page result count.

Can this support freedom-to-operate or competitive-landscape research?

It is well suited to scoping that work. Coverage across 100+ patent authorities, substructure search, assignee and inventor search, and the linked clinical-trial landscape make competitive-landscape and freedom-to-operate scoping fast. Results are a research aid, not a legal opinion: a freedom-to-operate conclusion requires qualified counsel and an appropriately scoped search, including sources and jurisdictions this corpus may not cover. For formal work, results flow into the full Design Your Invention platform, where prior art is saved with an append-only audit trail.

How many patents and jurisdictions are covered?

The public search corpus covers 120M+ patent records from 100+ patent authorities across IPC classes, sourced from the Google Patents public dataset via BigQuery. Coverage, full-text availability, language, and legal-status freshness vary by authority and by publication delay, so it is broad rather than complete. The in-app prior-art search inside the platform uses a separate data source, so result sets can differ.

How is this different from Google Patents or Lens?

Beyond keyword search, results carry an enrichment layer: compound chemistry with 2D structures, substructure search to find other patents in the corpus disclosing a scaffold, and a linked clinical-trial landscape. You can save patents to a portfolio, export to CSV, and move straight into a full IP management platform with its own integrated prior-art search.

Is my search activity private?

You can search without creating an account, and anonymous searches are not tied to a personal profile. Queries are still processed and logged for operational purposes such as rate limiting, abuse prevention, and service monitoring, as described in the privacy policy. When you sign in, your saved patents and portfolio are private to your account, and the wider platform is built for confidential invention workflows with tenant-scoped access controls.

Which databases power the enrichment?

Compound and trial data is drawn from established scientific sources: PubChem and SureChEMBL for compound chemistry, UniChem for cross-database identifiers, RDKit for structure depiction, and ClinicalTrials.gov for the trial landscape.

How do I run a prior art search before drafting an application?

Start with a free keyword, assignee, inventor, patent-number, or chemical-structure search to map the existing art, then save the relevant patents. Those saved references carry into the full Design Your Invention platform, where AI drafting generates draft claims with exactly those references available as context, against a frozen, auditable snapshot of what was reviewed. The draft and the search behind it both require attorney review.

Can I search Indian patents and other international jurisdictions?

Yes. The corpus spans 100+ patent authorities, including Indian (IN) patents alongside US, EP, WO, CN, JP, KR, and others, sourced from the Google Patents public dataset via BigQuery. You can filter any query by jurisdiction, and a free anonymous search already covers titles and abstracts worldwide; signing in with a work email adds full-text claims and CSV export.

## AI Patent Drafting Software With Attorney Review
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/ai-patent-drafting#main-content)

# AI Patent Drafting With Attorney Review Built In

An attorney-in-the-loop drafting assistant that turns invention details and saved prior art into a structured first draft for attorney review: claims, abstract, description, and novelty analysis, prepared for the drafting conventions of the target jurisdiction. AI drafts are dramatically better when they know the art on record.

## Drafts That Know the Prior Art

Without prior-art context, a model writes generic claims. With the relevant references in front of it, including pasted claim text, it drafts claims against the art on record, which the attorney then tests for novelty. Drafting lives inside the patent family, because that is how patent work flows.

### Prior Art Search

Worldwide patent search via EPO Open Patent Services, covering 100+ jurisdictions through INPADOC.

### Prior Art Management

Save, annotate, paste claim text, and track the relevance of references per patent family.

### AI Draft Generation

Feed invention details and saved prior art to an enterprise Claude model to generate jurisdiction-specific claims, abstract, description, and novelty analysis, asynchronously.

## Claims Written to the Rules That Apply

The drafting engine applies jurisdiction-specific claim format, statutory rules, and mandatory section structure. US, EP, IN, and PCT are the production set.

### USPTO

35 USC 101 / 112 and obviousness-type double patenting addressed, with the full US section structure (Field, Background, Summary, Brief Description of Drawings, Detailed Description).

### EPO

EPC Article 84 clarity, conciseness, and support, plus the EPC 2000 "compound for use" claim format.

### Indian Patent Office

Section 3(d) enhanced-efficacy considerations flagged for attorney review on pharma claims, the single most important rule for Indian pharma patents.

### WIPO (PCT)

Jurisdiction-neutral claims compatible with USPTO and EPO conventions, with national-phase amendments flagged for entry.

## Real Coverage, Stated Plainly

Search runs through EPO OPS, returning bibliographic data and family links worldwide. Full-text claims coverage is exactly as honest as it should be for a legal audience.

| Data | US | IN | EP | PCT |

| Bibliographic data (title, abstract, applicants, IPC/CPC, dates, family) |

| Full-text claims | Paste | Paste | via EPO | via EPO |

Provenance you can defend. Every AI revision is generated against a frozen, immutable snapshot of the exact prior-art set used at that moment. What art the AI saw when it wrote a given claim is always answerable, even years later and even if the live reference was later deleted.

## A Draft Is a Record, Not a Blob of Text

Every claim is its own record with a real dependency tree. Abstract, novelty analysis, and each description section are their own units. Every change to every unit is its own append-only revision, capturing who, when, why, AI versus manual, and what art the AI saw.

### Per-unit regeneration

Refine claim 3 without burning tokens regenerating claims 1, 2, and 4 through N. Each claim and section is its own record.

### Interactive refinement

Natural-language instructions ("broaden claim 2 to cover oral and IV administration") produce a new revision of one unit, not a full rewrite.

### Manual edits, never blocked

Attorney edits are revisioned identically to AI edits, distinguished only by a source field.

### Restore as a new revision

Restoring an earlier revision creates a new revision, never a deletion. History only grows.

### Cascade staleness

Editing claim 2 marks dependent claims, novelty analysis, and description sections stale. You decide what to regenerate, the system never does it for you.

### Diff and tree edits

Side-by-side comparison between any two revisions of any unit, plus reorder, reparent, split, and merge of claims.

Approval lock and branching. An approved draft is hard-locked. To change it, you branch a new version that carries forward all content with full lineage. "Approved" stays a strong signal, and a draft cannot be approved while any unit is stale.

Mandatory reason-for-change. Every revision carries a reason, system-filled for AI revisions, attorney-supplied for manual edits and restores. The field is never null.

## A Separate Model Reviews the Draft

After an enterprise Claude model generates the draft, a background review runs a separate, independent reviewer model as a judge over the claims, abstract, description, and novelty analysis, banding how well each unit is supported by the prior art on record so you can spend review time where it matters. The bands guide attorney attention; they are not a legal determination.

### Three honest bands

High, medium, or low per unit, describing how well the generated text is supported by the prior art on record, not a probability and not a legal opinion. The reviewer defaults to medium when uncertain; high must be affirmatively justified.

### Evidence-grounded

Every rating cites a specific claim number, quoted phrase, or publication number from the prior-art snapshot. No vague hand-waving.

### Progressive reveal

The draft is readable the instant generation completes; scores backfill seconds later while you read. No single long spinner.

### Prioritization, not a determination

Bands rank where attorney attention is most useful, and do not assess patentability, novelty, or filing readiness. They do not block export or approval, and are not shown to the end client.

## Built to Survive an Audit

AI drafting is governed by the same audit-first controls that protect the wider platform: tenant boundaries, retained evidence, controlled model use, and review history that stands up to enterprise procurement and regulated IP workflows.

Enterprise review

Controls designed for procurement, security questionnaires, and regulated IP teams.

Evidence retained

Every generated draft remains tied to the prior-art snapshot and review trail behind it.

Part 11-aligned patterns

Audit and change-control patterns follow 21 CFR Part 11 expectations. Validation stays with the customer.

### Tenant isolation

Each customer workspace is separated at the application and data layers. Tenant identity is verified before any drafting record, prior-art source, or portfolio item can be accessed.

### Append-only audit

Draft revisions, source references, and prior-art snapshots are preserved as append-only evidence, creating a review history that can be inspected later without being rewritten.

### AI-specific controls

Model access, prompt handling, and spending limits are governed per tenant. Generation and saving are controlled separately, with retention-limited provider settings and no personal data by default. Current provider retention terms are shared as part of security review.

## Five Permissions, Server-Enforced

Frontend gating is defense-in-depth only. The token-costing draft:generate permission is deliberately separate from draft:write, so admins control who can trigger paid AI calls.

| Action | Admin | Attorney | Paralegal | Read-only |

| Search patents (EPO) |

| Save / paste prior art |

| Fill invention details |

## The Attorney Is the Author. The AI Is the Assistant.

Every draft starts in DRAFT status and requires review before filing. The novelty analysis flags potential overlaps with the prior art, and per-claim refinement lets attorneys tighten one claim without re-running the whole draft. The UI and DOCX export carry the disclaimer "AI-generated content. Not legal advice."

## AI Drafting Questions

What the assistant does, and where the attorney stays in control.

Does the AI file patents or replace attorneys?

No. This is a professional tool for attorneys: the attorney is the author and the AI is the assistant. Every generated draft starts in DRAFT status and requires attorney review before any filing. The UI and the DOCX export carry the disclaimer "AI-generated content. Not legal advice."

Which jurisdictions are supported?

US, EP, IN, and PCT (WO) are the production set, each with jurisdiction-specific claim format, drafting rules, and mandatory section structure applied. A missing required section is flagged rather than silently omitted. JP and CN are planned and are not available yet.

How does prior art work for US and Indian patents without a claims API?

Bibliographic data is retrieved for all jurisdictions via EPO OPS. EP and PCT patents also return full-text claims directly from EPO. US and Indian patents have no reliable public claims API today, so a claims-retrieval helper guides the attorney to paste claim text from the source (USPTO ODP or InPASS). Pasted claims are stored on the reference and fed to the AI for novelty analysis.

Is my data used to train the AI?

No. Tenant data is sent to the model provider only during generation, under an enterprise API agreement that does not permit training on customer content. Prompts contain only invention details and public prior art, and no personal data unless the attorney puts it there. The retention and processing terms in force, along with the current provider and processing regions, are shared as part of security review.

How is a draft defensible in an audit?

Every AI revision is generated against a frozen snapshot of the exact prior-art set used at that moment, and revision history is append-only at the database layer. So "what art did the AI see when it wrote claim 3?" is always answerable, even years later and even if the live reference was later deleted.

What models power it?

Generation runs on enterprise Claude models from Anthropic, configured for confidential business workflows, and a separate background review runs a second, independent model as a judge to band the claims, abstract, description, and novelty analysis as high, medium, or low support. Model selection is governed by task, availability, and customer requirements, so exact versions change over time and are confirmed during security review rather than pinned in marketing copy.

Can paralegals trigger AI generation?

No. The draft:generate permission (which costs tokens) is deliberately separated from draft:write. Paralegals can search, save prior art, fill invention details, view drafts, and export, but only attorneys and tenant admins can generate, refine, or approve.

Is it suitable for regulated and pharma teams?

Yes. The append-only audit trail, electronic records, and access controls follow 21 CFR Part 11 patterns, and the India Section 3(d) enhanced-efficacy requirement is flagged for attorney review on pharma claims. The structured, versioned record is built to stand up in enterprise procurement and regulatory review. Compliance and validation still depend on your intended use, configuration, procedures, and quality system.

Can I just use ChatGPT to write my patent application?

A general chatbot writes generic claims with no access to the prior art on record, no jurisdiction-specific statutory rules, no version history, and no audit trail. This assistant grounds every draft in the actual prior art saved to the family (including pasted claim text), applies US, EP, IN, and PCT rules and section structure, runs a second-model confidence review, and keeps an append-only audit trail with mandatory attorney review before filing. The attorney is the author; the AI is the assistant.

Can the AI spot claim-support issues or weaknesses before filing?

Yes. Generation produces a novelty analysis that flags potential overlaps with the prior art on record, and a separate, independent reviewer model reviews each claim, the abstract, the description, and the novelty analysis, banding each as high, medium, or low support with a cited rationale. You see the least-supported sections first. It assists the review; the attorney makes the call.

Can it draft patent applications for India?

Yes. India (IN) is in the production jurisdiction set. Drafts apply Indian Patent Office rules, including the Section 3(d) enhanced-efficacy requirement that is decisive for pharma claims, plus the mandatory section structure, with US, EP, and PCT supported alongside it. A missing required section is flagged rather than silently omitted.

## Read the Rejection Limitation by Limitation

Each claim is broken into labeled limitations and charted against every reference the examiner relies on. See where the examiner’s mapping holds, where it is partial, and where it says nothing.

- 01 Deterministic claim parsing Claims are parsed without a model call. Numbering is never changed, and a multiple dependent claim keeps every dependency path.

- 02 Parse problems stop the chart Duplicate or unnumbered claims and structural dependency errors, such as circular or unresolved references, are raised as blockers until the parse is corrected.

- 03 One reading per limitation, per reference Each cited passage carries its own pinpoint, and every quotation is matched to the source text before it is stored.

- 04 Silence is not a finding A limitation the examiner did not address is marked not addressed. It is never presented as proof the reference lacks it.

## Choose a Strategy for Every Ground of Rejection

Every issue in the signed analysis gets a recorded strategy before the drafting starts. The choice shapes the response sections, and the reasoning stays with the issue for the reviewing attorney.

### From Ground of Rejection to Response Section

Anticipation

§ 102 · Claims 1-3

Remarks addressing the cited disclosure

Counsel records the disputed limitation and the basis for the response.

Indefiniteness

§ 112(b) · Claim 4

Claim amendment and supporting remarks

The revised language stays linked to its as-filed disclosure support.

Illustrative attorney-selected strategies · Available choices depend on the issue type.

### Amend and traverse

Narrow the claims and argue the rejection does not apply to them as amended.

### Amend the claims

Overcome the issue by amendment, with the inserted language linked to support in the application as filed.

### Traverse the rejection

Contest the examiner’s position without amendment, in remarks built on the record.

### File a terminal disclaimer

Answer a nonstatutory double patenting rejection. Not offered against statutory double patenting.

### Rewrite in independent form as indicated

Take up allowable subject matter in an objected-to claim. The rewrite is computed and previewed before you accept it.

Counsel decides. Only strategies the US rule pack permits for the issue type are offered, and only an attorney selects one.

## Office Action Questions

Coverage, documents, and how your team stays in control.

Which office actions are supported?

Analysis reads USPTO communications including non-final and final rejections, advisory actions, and restriction and election requirements. A notice of allowance is recognized, with nothing to map. The response workspace supports replies under 37 CFR 1.111 and amendments after final under 37 CFR 1.116. Other jurisdictions are planned, starting with EP. RCE submissions, pre-appeal requests, and restriction responses are not yet supported.

How do I bring in the documents?

Import a US application by application, patent, or publication number, or upload your documents. The analysis identifies the office action, examined claims, and available references. You confirm the record when a document or claim set is ambiguous. Missing or unreadable pages are flagged for review.

Which reference documents can it read?

EP and WO publication text is fetched through EPO OPS, and US published applications through USPTO Open Data. Granted US patents and non-patent literature require an uploaded copy. The examiner’s PTO-892 reference list can be fetched to the case, but is not read by the analysis.

Can AI help draft arguments and amendments?

Model-assisted issue restatements, amendment proposals, amendment assessments, and anticipation arguments are available only where the capability has completed its evaluation, the deployment enables it, and workspace policy permits it. The structured response workspace, claim listing, support links, and exports work without these drafting aids. Attorneys choose strategies and accept changes, and model-derived text cannot be approved until it passes an automated independent review.

Who reviews and approves the work?

An authorized attorney signs the analysis after confirming their identity, and whoever last corrected the map cannot sign it. Response approval requires an authorized attorney who did not last revise the draft. Corrections and decisions are recorded with a reason, and approved content is locked. Model-derived response text must also pass an automated independent review, a separate model reading plus code checks, before approval.

What can I export, and does the software file?

Word exports include analysis review drafts, evidence reports, signed issue maps, response review drafts, approved filing copies, and interview agendas. The attorney files separately in Patent Center and records the filing. The software does not submit the response to the USPTO.

Does it stay connected to the patent docket?

Yes. The office action, analysis, and response belong to the docketed matter. Candidate response dates come from the docketing rules engine and require attorney confirmation; analysis does not overwrite the docket’s due date. Workspace policies and matter access controls apply throughout.

## Design Your Invention vs Legacy IPMS
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/compare#main-content)

# One IP Platform Instead of Four Disconnected Tools

Most IP teams run a docketing system, a separate prior art search tool, a drafting tool, and spreadsheets for chemistry and fees. Design Your Invention is an intellectual property management software (IPMS) platform that unifies all of it for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms, on an audit-first, Part 11-aligned architecture.

## What a Modern IPMS Includes by Default

Legacy IP management software is strong at docketing but usually stops there. The capabilities below are the ones pharma and boutique IP teams most often bolt on with extra tools, and the ones Design Your Invention includes in one platform.

| Capability | Typical legacy setup | Design Your Invention |

| Multi-jurisdiction docketing | Core strength of most legacy IPMS tools | US, PCT, EU, JP, CN, and IN docketing with PCT/PRV/NPE case linkage in a visual family tree |

| Prior art search | Commonly a separate subscription or manual EPO/Espacenet searches | Built in, querying the EPO global database across 100+ patent authorities without leaving the family view |

| AI-assisted patent drafting | Typically not part of a docketing platform | First-draft generation for attorney review across US, EP, IN, and PCT (WO), with a mandatory review workflow |

| Office action analysis and response | Usually worked in Word documents and email, outside the docket | USPTO rejections mapped to claims with source-checked quotes, and responses built on the signed analysis for approval by a second attorney |

| Drug and chemistry enrichment | Rarely addressed; handled in separate tools or spreadsheets | Chemistry-aware enrichment aimed at pharma IP workflows |

| Part 11-aligned architecture | Varies widely by vendor and product age | Audit-first design following FDA 21 CFR Part 11 patterns: reason-for-change, append-only audit trail, e-signature re-authentication |

| Multi-tenant data isolation | Depends on deployment model | Per-tenant isolation enforced at the database level with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security |

Legacy IP management products vary widely by vendor and product generation. This comparison describes the common multi-tool setup, not any single named platform. Pricing is not published; contact us for current pricing.

## Comparison Questions

How Design Your Invention fits next to the IP management tools teams already know.

What are the alternatives to legacy IPMS tools like Clarivate, Anaqua, or AppColl for pharma IP?

Teams evaluating alternatives to established IP management platforms typically want fewer disconnected tools. Design Your Invention is a modern option built for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms that unifies multi-jurisdiction patent docketing, prior art search, AI-assisted drafting, office action analysis and response, and chemistry enrichment in one connected, audit-trailed platform, rather than stitching a docketing tool together with separate search and drafting subscriptions.

How is Design Your Invention different from legacy IP management software?

The main difference is consolidation. Many IP teams run a docketing system, a separate prior art search tool, a drafting tool, and spreadsheets for chemistry and fees. Design Your Invention brings docketing, prior art search across 100+ patent authorities, AI-assisted drafting for US, EP, IN, and PCT, USPTO office action analysis and response, and chemistry enrichment into one connected, audit-trailed platform with a Part 11-aligned architecture and tenant-scoped data isolation.

Does Design Your Invention replace a separate prior art search tool?

For most prior art work, yes. The platform queries the EPO global patent database covering 100+ patent authorities directly inside the patent family view, with keyword, inventor, applicant, and patent-number search modes. Results save to the family with relevance scoring and attorney notes, creating an auditable prior art record without a second subscription.

Is Design Your Invention a good fit for IP boutique law firms?

Yes. IP boutique law firms are one of the two core audiences, alongside pharma companies. The platform is built for small and mid-sized IP teams that need multi-jurisdiction docketing, deadline and fee tracking, prior art search, and a defensible audit trail without the cost and complexity of the largest enterprise suites.

Does Design Your Invention include AI patent drafting that legacy tools usually lack?

Yes. AI-assisted drafting is built in and generates a first draft for attorney review across US, EP, IN, and PCT (WO), each with jurisdiction-specific drafting rules, with JP and CN planned. Every draft carries a mandatory disclaimer and a draft to in-review to approved workflow, so no AI-generated content can be exported or filed without human sign-off. It is a starting point for attorneys, not filing-ready output.

Does Design Your Invention handle office action responses?

Yes, for USPTO office actions. The platform maps each rejection to the affected claims and the cited passages, with every quotation matched to the source text, and an attorney signs the analysis. The response is built on that signed analysis with a strategy per issue, a claim listing, and support links to the application as filed, then approved by an attorney who did not last revise it and exported to Word for filing. Legacy setups usually handle this work in Word and email, outside the docket. Other jurisdictions are planned, starting with EP.

# IP Management Software, Answered

What Design Your Invention is, who it is for, the jurisdictions it covers, and how it handles prior art search, AI-assisted patent drafting, office action analysis and response, FDA 21 CFR Part 11 aligned controls, and security. If your question is not here, book a demo and ask.

What is Design Your Invention?

Design Your Invention (DYI) is an intellectual property management software (IPMS) platform for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms. It brings multi-jurisdiction patent docketing, prior art search across 100+ patent authorities via the EPO, and AI-assisted patent drafting for US, EP, IN, and PCT (WO) into one connected, audit-trailed workspace. The architecture follows FDA 21 CFR Part 11 patterns, with tenant-scoped data isolation so each organization keeps its portfolio separate.

Is the platform generally available or in private beta?

The full IP management platform is in private beta and under active development, so features can change during the beta. The public patent search tool is live and free to use today. If you want early access to the platform, book a demo or use the contact form and we will talk through your workflow and the current beta scope.

Who is Design Your Invention for?

DYI is built for pharma companies and IP boutique law firms that manage patent portfolios across multiple jurisdictions. Typical users include IP attorneys, patent paralegals, IP directors, and legal operations teams who need patent docketing, prior art search, fee and deadline tracking, and a defensible audit trail in one place, instead of spreadsheets and email.

What is IP management software?

IP management software is a specialized platform that helps law firms, corporations, and patent teams manage their intellectual property portfolios, including patent applications, PCT filings, office actions, deadlines, fees, and compliance requirements. It replaces spreadsheets and email-based tracking with a structured, searchable, and auditable system.

Which controls support an FDA 21 CFR Part 11-aligned workflow?

Every edit to a critical field requires a documented reason-for-change. The audit trail logs who made each change, what changed, and when, and is append-only: the application exposes no edit or delete path on audit history. Electronic approvals require re-authentication, and role-based access control limits who can perform sensitive actions. These are product capabilities, not a compliance certification. Validation and Part 11 compliance depend on each customer intended use, configuration, procedures, training, and quality system.

Can I manage PCT and PRV filings in one place?

Yes. The platform links PRV (provisional), PCT (international), and NPE (national phase entry) cases to their parent patent families. You can see the entire filing hierarchy in a visual family tree, track deadlines across all filing types, and manage office actions and fees from a single dashboard.

Can the platform manage patents across multiple jurisdictions?

Yes. Multi-jurisdiction portfolios are the core use case. Docketing covers US, PCT, EP, JP, CN, and IN, with PRV, PCT, and NPE cases linked to their parent application families so the full filing hierarchy is visible in one place. Deadlines, fees, and office actions are tracked across every jurisdiction in your portfolio, and fee analytics roll up spend with date-accurate multi-currency conversion into one reporting currency.

How does the platform help reduce deadline risk?

Supported statutory and procedural deadlines are derived from your case data rather than entered by hand, so they do not depend on someone remembering to add them to a calendar. Every deadline gets a 0 to 100 risk score with green, amber, and red levels, and automated email digests push what is due to the responsible owner before the date. A weekly stale-alert report also surfaces cases that are quietly going wrong without generating a hard deadline. Calculated dates are workflow aids: coverage depends on the case data you record, and a qualified patent professional remains responsible for verifying every date.

What patent fee types are supported?

The platform supports 42 fee types across 8 categories, including filing fees, examination fees, issue fees, maintenance/annuity fees, extension fees, petition fees, PCT fees, and miscellaneous fees. Each fee can be tracked as due, paid, waived, or overdue with full analytics and CSV export.

Is the platform multi-tenant?

Yes. Each organization gets a dedicated subdomain (e.g., yourfirm.designyourinvention.com) with tenant-scoped data. Isolation is enforced at the database level using Row-Level Security (RLS) inside tenant-scoped transactions, which is designed to prevent cross-organization access. Your organization data is kept separate from every other organization on the platform.

How does role-based access control work?

The platform supports four roles: Tenant Admin, Attorney, Paralegal, and Viewer. Each role has granular permissions. For example, Viewers can browse and search but cannot create, edit, or delete records. Permissions are enforced both in the UI and on the server, so access control cannot be bypassed.

Can I export my data?

Yes. Every list view (families, PRV applications, PCT filings, NPE cases, fees, and audit logs) supports one-click CSV export with all columns included. You can also use bulk actions to select multiple records for status changes or deletion with a single operation.

What security measures are in place?

The platform uses Auth0 for authentication with support for SSO, SAML, and multi-factor authentication. Access tokens are held in memory rather than written to browser storage, data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and documents are stored in encrypted S3 buckets with presigned URL access. High-risk actions require step-up re-authentication. Independent security assurance reports, such as SOC 2, have not been issued yet, and we will say so plainly in any security review.

Can I import my existing patent portfolio from spreadsheets?

Yes. You can upload your existing Excel or CSV file and the system validates every row before anything touches the database. You get a color-coded preview showing which families will be created, which filings will be merged, and which will be skipped. One click to confirm, and all records are created in a single atomic transaction with full audit trail. Up to 5,000 filings per import.

What integrations are available?

The platform is a cloud-based web application that runs entirely in your browser, with no installation or plugins required. It supports CSV export for every list view, presigned S3 document downloads, and Auth0 SSO integration for enterprise identity providers including SAML and OAuth 2.0. A REST API is available for custom integrations with existing firm systems.

Is Design Your Invention cloud-based or on-premise?

Design Your Invention is a cloud-based web application that runs in your browser, with nothing to install or maintain. Each organization gets a dedicated subdomain with fully isolated data, enforced at the database level with Row-Level Security. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and documents are stored in encrypted storage with presigned access.

Is AI-generated patent drafting safe for filing?

AI-generated drafts are a starting point, not a final filing. AI-generated content may be incomplete or inaccurate and is not legal advice, so every draft carries a mandatory disclaimer and requires attorney review. The platform enforces a status workflow (draft, in review, approved), so no AI-generated content can be exported or acted on without human sign-off. Prior art snapshots, model details, and token counts are preserved for every generation, giving you a complete record of what the assistant saw and produced.

Which jurisdictions does AI patent drafting support?

Four jurisdictions are in the production set: US (USPTO, 35 USC 101/112), EP (EPO, EPC Article 84 and the EPC 2000 compound-for-use format), IN (Indian Patent Office, Section 3(d)/(i)/(j)/(k) exclusions), and WO (WIPO/PCT, international-stage neutral drafting). JP and CN are planned and not available yet. Each supported jurisdiction has drafting guidance and mandatory section structure applied during generation, so claim format and section coverage follow local convention, with relevant statutory considerations flagged for attorney review.

How does prior art search work in the platform?

The in-app prior art search queries the EPO global patent database (Open Patent Services) covering 100+ patent authorities, without leaving your patent family view. It is a separate data source from the free public search tool, so result sets can differ. Four search modes are available: Keywords (technical terms across titles and abstracts), Inventor (handles name variations and titles), Applicant (strips corporate suffixes automatically), and Patent Number (any format, kind codes handled). Results can be filtered by IPC classification, date range, and jurisdiction. Relevant patents are saved directly to your family with relevance scoring and attorney notes, creating an auditable prior art record.

How does office action analysis and response work?

Office action analysis reads a USPTO office action, once an attorney confirms the documents, into an issue map with the legal basis, affected claims, and cited references for each issue, and charts every claim limitation against the cited passages. Every quotation is matched to the source text before it is stored, and an authorized attorney signs the analysis. The response is then built on the signed analysis: a strategy for every issue, a claim listing with status identifiers, and support for inserted claim language in the application as filed. Replies under 37 CFR 1.111 and amendments after final under 37 CFR 1.116 are supported. Approval requires an attorney who did not last revise the draft, approved content is locked, and the reply exports to Word for the attorney to file. AI drafting aids are available only where the capability has completed its evaluation and workspace policy permits it. Other jurisdictions are planned, starting with EP.

Does the platform support pharmaceutical patent workflows?

Yes. Pharma companies are one of the two core audiences. Prior art search resolves detected compounds to canonical chemical structures and supports substructure search, which matters for chemistry and life-sciences portfolios. AI-assisted drafting applies Indian Patent Office drafting rules and flags the Section 3 exclusions that shape pharma patentability for attorney review, and the audit-first architecture follows FDA 21 CFR Part 11 patterns for regulated workflows.

How do I choose the right patent management software?

Look for a platform that covers your whole workflow in one place rather than a docketing tool plus separate prior art and drafting subscriptions. Practical criteria are multi-jurisdiction docketing, automatic deadline derivation, fee and renewal tracking, built-in prior art search, office action analysis connected to the docket, an easy way to import an existing portfolio, and an audit trail and access control that meet your compliance needs. Design Your Invention is built to cover all of these in a single platform, with a capability-by-capability breakdown on the comparison page.

How much does Design Your Invention cost?

Pricing is not published yet and is tailored to your team size and portfolio. Book a demo or use the contact form and we will share current pricing for your situation. We keep pricing out of marketing until it is final and public, so a quote reflects what actually applies to your team.

How does Design Your Invention compare to legacy tools like Anaqua, Clarivate, or AppColl?

Most IP teams run a docketing system plus separate tools for prior art search and drafting, with spreadsheets for chemistry and fees. Design Your Invention unifies multi-jurisdiction docketing, prior art search across 100+ patent authorities, AI-assisted drafting for US, EP, IN, and PCT, USPTO office action analysis and response, and chemistry enrichment in one connected, audit-trailed platform. The comparison page has a capability-by-capability breakdown against the typical legacy setup.

Is my content used to train AI models?

No. Invention details and prior art are sent to the model provider only to generate the draft you asked for, under an enterprise API agreement that does not permit training on customer content. Prompts carry no personal data unless an attorney puts it there, every generation is recorded against a frozen prior-art snapshot, and the retention terms, provider, and processing regions in force are shared as part of security review.

What security certifications does Design Your Invention hold?

None yet, and we will not imply otherwise. The security program is being built around the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, but no SOC 2 Type I or Type II report has been issued and no independent security audit has been completed. What exists today is architectural: tenant-scoped authorization with database row-level security, role-based access control, encryption in transit and at rest, append-only audit history, and step-up authentication on high-risk actions.

## After a Final Rejection: Choosing Between 1.116, Appeal, and RCE Without AFCP 2.0
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/blog/after-final-rejection-options-uspto#main-content)

A final rejection changes the question from "what should we argue?" to "which path should this application take?" For years, many practitioners answered with the After Final Consideration Pilot 2.0, which gave examiners extra time to consider a modest after-final amendment at no fee. The USPTO ended that program, and the last requests were accepted on December 14, 2024. The remaining paths are older, more formal, and each one starts its own chain of deadlines.

This guide compares the options after a USPTO final rejection, an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116, an examiner interview, a notice of appeal with or without pre-appeal review, and a request for continued examination, and sets out what each path means for the docket. It is general information about US practice, not legal advice for any particular matter.

## What "Final" Actually Closes

A final rejection closes prosecution on the merits. The applicant can still reply, but a reply to a final action that does not place the application in condition for allowance does not stop the clock. The period for reply keeps running, typically three months from the action, extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) up to the six-month statutory limit, until the applicant files a notice of appeal, files a request for continued examination, or receives an allowance.

The examiner's advisory action, which answers an after-final reply, does not restart that period. Its timing does matter for extension fees: if the reply was filed within two months of the final action, extension fees are computed from the advisory action's mail date rather than from the original period. That rule, and the rest of the response chain, is covered in our guide to USPTO office action response deadlines.

## Option 1: An Amendment Under 37 CFR 1.116

After a final rejection, amendments are entered at the examiner's discretion and only within limits. Under 37 CFR 1.116, an amendment may be admitted if it cancels claims, complies with a requirement of form expressly set out in a previous action, or presents rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal. An amendment that touches the merits in any other way needs a showing of good and sufficient reasons why it is necessary and was not presented earlier.

In practice, the after-final amendments most likely to be entered are the simple ones: canceling rejected claims, rewriting a dependent claim the examiner indicated was allowable into independent form, or fixing a formal objection. An amendment that adds a new limitation requiring further search will often be refused, and without AFCP 2.0 there is no dedicated program that gives the examiner extra time to search it.

## Option 2: An Examiner Interview

Interviews after a final rejection are at the examiner's discretion, but an interview that may advance the application toward allowance or narrow the issues for appeal is commonly granted. Requests can be made through the USPTO's Automated Interview Request form. A short agenda and proposed claim language sent ahead make the time productive, and the interview often tells you which of the remaining paths is realistic.

An interview does not extend or toll the period for reply. It is a way to choose a path, not a path of its own, so it should be scheduled well inside the window that still allows a reply, an appeal, or an RCE to be filed in time.

## Option 3: A Notice of Appeal, With or Without Pre-Appeal Review

A notice of appeal under 37 CFR 41.31 is filed within the period for reply to the final action, with extensions available under 37 CFR 1.136(a). The appeal brief is then due two months from the filing of the notice under 37 CFR 41.37, and that period can itself be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

The pre-appeal brief request for review remains available. It is filed together with the notice of appeal, is limited to five pages of argument, and asks a review panel to review whether the rejection has a clear error or lacks an essential element of a prima facie case. It is not a vehicle for amendments. The panel can send the appeal forward, reopen prosecution, or allow the application. If the appeal proceeds, the time for the brief is reset to one month from the panel's decision or the balance of the original two-month period, whichever is longer.

Appeal suits disputes about how the art or the claims should be read, where another round of argument before the same examiner is unlikely to change the outcome. A successful appeal can also earn patent term adjustment for the time spent in appellate review.

## Option 4: A Request for Continued Examination

A request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 requires a submission, such as an amendment, arguments, or new evidence, plus the RCE fee. It withdraws the finality of the rejection and reopens prosecution, so the submission is considered on the merits. Fees increase for a second and later RCE.

The RCE is often the default choice, and sometimes it is the right one: it is the only after-final path that guarantees full consideration of a substantive amendment or new evidence. It carries a patent term cost, however. Time spent in continued examination is excluded from the three-year pendency guarantee in the patent term adjustment calculation, so an RCE can reduce the term a granted patent would otherwise earn.

## Docketing Each Path

Each path generates its own dates, and a final rejection should be docketed with all of them visible so the choice of path is made with the calendar in view:

- The final action chain - the period for reply, the two-month date that preserves favorable advisory action timing, the extension ladder, and the six-month statutory limit.

- The appeal chain - the notice of appeal date, the appeal brief due two months later, and, after the examiner's answer, the reply brief period.

- The pre-appeal reset - when a pre-appeal decision issues, the brief date recomputed from the decision.

- The RCE follow-up - once an RCE is filed, the final action chain closes and the matter waits for the next action on the merits.

- The term companion date - the three-month target that avoids applicant delay for patent term adjustment, shown as advisory alongside the legal deadline.

When a path is taken, the dates that belong to the other paths should close together, with the closure recorded, a discipline we cover in our guide to de-docketing.

## How Design Your Invention Fits After a Final Rejection

Design Your Invention's patent docketing platform computes the office action response chain from the recorded action under versioned, cited rules, including the extension ladder, the statutory limit, and the patent term companion date, with every computed date subject to attorney review.

The office action analysis and response workspace reads final rejections and advisory actions into a signed issue map, using the method in our guide to analyzing a USPTO office action. The response workspace supports amendments after final under 37 CFR 1.116 as well as replies under 37 CFR 1.111, with the claim listing and support checks described in our claim amendments guide. Notices of appeal, pre-appeal requests, and RCE submissions are prepared outside the response workspace today.

After a final rejection, the argument matters less than the path. Choose the path with the issue map and the docket both in view.

## Claim Amendments Under 37 CFR 1.121: Status Identifiers, Markings, and Support
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/blog/claim-amendments-37-cfr-1-121-guide#main-content)

A claim amendment can be substantively right and still go nowhere. A wrong status identifier, markings shown against the wrong version, or a canceled claim reproduced in full can draw a notice of non-compliant amendment, and an inserted phrase without support in the application as filed can draw a new matter rejection. Neither problem has anything to do with whether the amended claim is patentable.

This guide covers the mechanics of amending claims in a reply to a USPTO office action: the claim listing required by 37 CFR 1.121, the status identifiers, how changes are marked, how to show written description support, and what to recheck once the claims change. It is general information about US practice, not legal advice for any particular matter.

## The Claim Listing: Every Claim, Every Time

Under 37 CFR 1.121(c), claims are amended by rewriting the entire claim with its changes marked, inside a complete claim listing. The listing replaces every earlier version of the claims in the application, so it must include every claim ever presented, in ascending numerical order, each with a status identifier in parentheses.

Canceled and not entered claims are listed by number and status only, without their text, and consecutive claims with the same status can be grouped, for example "Claims 5-7 (Canceled)". New claims are numbered consecutively from the highest number previously presented under 37 CFR 1.126, so a canceled claim's number is never reused.

## The Status Identifiers

Each claim in the listing carries one identifier describing its status as of this amendment:

- Original - the claim as filed, never amended.

- Currently amended - changed in this paper, with the changes marked.

- Previously presented - added or amended in an earlier paper that was entered, and unchanged now.

- New - added in this paper, presented without markings.

- Canceled - removed, listed without text.

- Withdrawn - withdrawn from consideration, typically after a restriction requirement. A withdrawn claim being changed is shown as withdrawn and currently amended, with markings.

- Not entered - presented in an earlier paper that the examiner did not enter, listed without text.

Most identifier mistakes come from tracking status by memory. A claim amended in the last reply is "Previously presented" now, not "Currently amended". A claim from an after-final amendment that was never entered still sits at its last entered version. And homemade labels such as "Previously amended" invite a notice even where the Office has tolerated nonstandard identifiers in the past. The listed set is the safe set.

## Markings: Show Changes Against the Last Entered Version

A currently amended claim shows its changes against the immediately prior version of that claim, which means the last version actually entered, not the claim as originally filed and not a draft that was never filed. Added text is underlined and deleted text is shown in strike-through. Double brackets may be used instead to delete five or fewer consecutive characters, or where strike-through would be hard to see.

> 1. (Currently amended) A sensor system comprising: a temperature sensor; a controller configured to adjust a sampling interval; and a stored calibration profile that maps each temperature band to a sampling interval.

Two consistency checks prevent most marking errors. Every claim marked "Currently amended" should show at least one change, and no claim with any other identifier should show markings. A claim whose markings were generated against the wrong baseline is the hardest error to spot by eye, which is why the baseline should come from the prosecution record rather than a local file.

## Support in the Application as Filed

Under 35 U.S.C. 132(a), no amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure, and amended claims must still satisfy the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The MPEP asks applicants to point out where the support for an amendment can be found, and doing so in the remarks is the simplest way to avoid a new matter rejection.

- Cite support per inserted phrase - a paragraph or page and line for each piece of new claim language, not one citation for the whole amendment.

- Remember the original claims - claims as filed are part of the disclosure and can supply support of their own.

- Watch negative limitations - excluding something requires support for the exclusion, not just silence in the specification.

- Check carved-out ranges - a narrower numerical range needs support for its new endpoints, not merely for the broader range.

- Avoid paraphrase - wording that is close to the specification but not in it is exactly where support disputes start.

## What Changes When the Claims Change

Amending one claim ripples through the rest of the listing. Before the reply is filed, recheck:

- Antecedent basis - an amendment that renames or removes an element can leave "the" or "said" references in dependent claims pointing at nothing, which invites an indefiniteness rejection.

- Dependency - claims that depend on a canceled claim need to be amended or canceled, and new dependent claims need a valid parent.

- Excess claim fees - fees under 37 CFR 1.16(h) and (i) apply for each independent claim over three and each claim over twenty, with a separate fee for multiple dependent claims, and an amendment that pushes the counts above what has already been paid owes the difference.

- After-final limits - once an action is final, amendments are entered only within the limits of 37 CFR 1.116, which we cover in our guide to options after a final rejection.

- Prosecution history - narrowing amendments made for patentability can limit equivalents later, so each one should be a deliberate choice.

The remarks should also explain how the amended claims avoid each cited reference. Under 37 CFR 1.111(c), an applicant who amends in reply to a rejection must clearly point out the patentable novelty the claims present in view of the art, which is why the amendment decision belongs in the office action analysis rather than at the end of drafting.

## How Design Your Invention Handles the Claim Listing

The office action response workspace in Design Your Invention builds the claim listing from the examined claims in the prosecution record, so markings are always shown against the right baseline. Each claim carries its status, and claims are parsed deterministically, including multiple dependent claims and Markush groups. Possible antecedent basis gaps are flagged on every claim change, and excess-claim counts update as the listing changes.

Inserted language is linked to passages in the application as filed, which an attorney confirms, and added words that no cited passage holds are flagged before approval. The response is approved by an attorney who did not last revise it, approved content is locked, and the reply is exported to Word for the attorney to file. When AI assists with amendment proposals, the same support checks apply, as we explain in our guide to using AI on office action responses.

An amendment is a legal argument written in claim language. Get the listing, the markings, and the support right, and the examiner is left with only the argument to answer.

## Using AI on Office Action Responses: What the USPTO Expects
[Skip to content](https://designyourinvention.com/blog/ai-office-action-response-uspto-guidance#main-content)

Generative AI has moved from patent drafting into prosecution. Attorneys now use it to summarize office actions, restate rejections, propose claim amendments, and draft first versions of arguments. The USPTO has not banned any of that. It has, however, been clear that every existing obligation of the person who signs the response still applies, and that relying on an AI tool is not a substitute for the signer's own review.
